contents.name: Posterior density as prior times likelihood divided by marginal evidence
contents.support: The text identifies p(y) as the sum or integral of prior times likelihood and states the normalized posterior formula. The item additionally defines a fixed-fiber update for any sigma-finite measure and states exactly when the quotient is left undefined.

contents.name: Improper flat prior for a known-variance normal mean; posterior proper with at least one observation
contents.support: The source gives the n≥1 normal-mean result. The example independently completes the square and evaluates the finite positive evidence, retaining the exact known-variance and n≥1 assumptions.

contents.name: Improper Beta(0,0) prior produces an improper binomial posterior at y=0 or y=n
contents.support: The text states the endpoint failure. The example supplies complete lower-bound integral arguments for both endpoints and separately verifies sigma-finiteness of the prior.

contents.name: Improper posterior densities require a finite normalizing integral check
contents.support: The source motivates checking the posterior integral. The proposition proves for an arbitrary measurable nonnegative section that a finite positive normalizer is necessary and sufficient for probability normalization.

item_arguments.argument: Define the extended nonnegative evidence integral for each measurable likelihood section. Define the quotient update only on finite positive fibers and explicitly make no predictive-probability claim for an improper prior.
The likelihood-weighted integral is a measure of total mass Z. A finite positive scalar multiple is a probability exactly when cZ=1, which is equivalent to 0<Z<infinity and c=1/Z.
Directly sum the two prior-weighted likelihoods at y=1; the evidence is 1/3 and the two normalized posterior masses are 1/2.
Compute m(0)=m(1)=1/2 and m(2)=0 in the finite deterministic model; the quotient at 2 is 0/0, while the published theorem provides a prior filler version on this marginal-null fiber.

Define the product sample density with respect to the recursively constructed product Lebesgue measure. Normalize each one-coordinate normal density by affine Lebesgue change of variables; use Tonelli inductively to show the product density has total mass one, then define its measure and verify the rectangle factorization identifies the independent product sampling law. Verify the flat Lebesgue prior is sigma-finite and infinite, complete the square, evaluate the fixed-data evidence by affine Lebesgue change of variables, and identify the normalized Borel posterior as N(y-bar, sigma-squared/n). AC supplies the countable-choice premises of the cited Lebesgue and normal-law suppliers.

Verify sigma-finiteness on compact subintervals and infinite prior mass by dyadic interval lower bounds. Multiply the Beta(0,0) prior by the binomial likelihood and use reflected dyadic interval bounds to prove infinite evidence at y=0 and y=n. The Lebesgue-measure branch is explicitly under AC.
